reason: The opcodes, branch ranges and the in-place semantics hold. X is still the row at sky_draw.next_row, sky_row leaves A = sky_skip = 0 when Z is set, the whole-row unroll by 4 relies on Y+1 being a multiple of 4 just as sky_draw.whole already does, sky_zero's branches all stay in page &31, and sky_k (&317A+9) does not start crossing a page. The problem is the net +5 bytes. They move sky_img0 from &317F to &3184, so helicopter 0's blocks (SKY_BLOCK &70) go from &317F/&31EF/&325F/&32CF to &3184/&31F4/&3264/&32D4. Blocks 1 and 3 straddle a page, so the hot LDA (d_ptr),Y reads in sky_draw.whole and line8 change which loads take the +1. d_ptr is block + 8*sky_d1 + sky_rc, and sky_rc is STZ'd for a row's first entry. For a fully drawn image (offset 0) a read crosses when Y >= 17 at present and when Y >= 12 after the move. That is 5 more page-crossing reads, +5 cycles, on every drawn row of block 1 or 3 of helicopter 0. Offsets 12-16 go the other way. The candidate itself calls this an unknown +/- cost and does not count it. sky_draw's next_row runs about 1.7 times a pass, so the extra crossings could plausibly eat a large share of the claimed 8.9 cycles a pass, or all of it. The saving is not established. The move also shifts per-screen data, which the skill's rule forbids ('No data moves').
